dish.title: Austrian Pork Schnitzel with Warm Viennese Potato Salad and Lemon
dish.description: Pork loin cutlets pounded thin, coated in flour, egg, and fine breadcrumbs, and shallow-fried in oil until puffed and golden, served with lemon wedges and a warm Viennese potato salad of sliced Yukon Gold potatoes, red onion, and chives in a tangy vinegar-mustard dressing.

recipe_version.title: Austrian Pork Schnitzel with Warm Viennese Potato Salad and Lemon
recipe_version.description: Pork loin cutlets pounded thin, coated in flour, egg, and fine breadcrumbs, and shallow-fried in oil until puffed and golden, served with lemon wedges and a warm Viennese potato salad of sliced Yukon Gold potatoes, red onion, and chives in a tangy vinegar-mustard dressing.

ingredients.name: boneless pork loin cutlets
ingredients.display_name: boneless center-cut pork loin cutlets (4 pieces)

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: 1 1/2 tsp potato water, 1/2 tsp dressing, 1/2 tsp pork

ingredients.name: plain fine dry breadcrumbs
ingredients.display_name: plain fine dry breadcrumbs whose label lists wheat flour, yeast, and salt only
ingredients.note: If you cannot find them: before you start, pulse about 6 oz day-old plain bakery bread whose label lists only wheat flour, water, yeast, and salt to fine crumbs in a food processor and dry them in a 12-inch skillet over medium, stirring, about 8 minutes; cool before breading. This adds about 12 minutes before step 1.

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Peel the potatoes and slice them 1/4 inch thick. Finely chop the red onion, chop the chives, and cut the lemon into wedges. Pound the cutlets between sheets of plastic wrap to an even 1/4 inch and season with 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper.

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.body: Put the potato slices, 6 cups water, and 1 1/2 tsp salt in a 4-quart pot, cover, and bring to a boil over high, about 9 minutes to come to a boil. Uncover and simmer until just tender, about 8 minutes. Drain in the colander.

steps.title: Bread the cutlets
steps.body: While the potatoes cook (overlap stated): set out 3 shallow dishes with the flour, the eggs beaten smooth, and the breadcrumbs. Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, and lay it in the crumbs, turning it once without pressing, so the coating stays loose. Set on the rack.

steps.title: Dress the potatoes
steps.body: In a 1-quart saucepan bring 1/3 cup water, the vinegar, mustard, sugar, and 1/2 tsp salt just to a simmer, about 1 minute. Pour it over the warm potatoes in a bowl, add the red onion and dressing oil, and fold gently until creamy-looking.

steps.title: Shallow-fry the schnitzel
steps.body: Heat the oil in a 12-inch heavy skillet over medium-high to 340 F, about 5 minutes. Shallow-fry 2 cutlets at a time, swirling the pan so the oil washes over the tops and the crust puffs, until deep golden, about 2 minutes per side and 145 F inside. Drain on the rack and repeat (2 batches).

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Fold the chives into the potato salad. Plate each schnitzel with a lemon wedge and the potato salad alongside.

equipment: wire rack set on a sheet pan

The breadcrumbs are a store-bought hard contract: the label lists wheat flour, yeast, and salt, with no milk, butter, soy, or sesame. The homemade fallback uses bread whose label lists only wheat flour, water, yeast, and salt.
Mustard (Dijon) has no FlavorWeave allergen token; disclosed here and in runtime_enum_gaps.
No milk, soy, sesame, fish, shellfish, or nuts.

scaling_notes.1: One cutlet fried alone in a 10-inch skillet; a quarter of the potatoes in a 2-quart pot with 3 cups water.
scaling_notes.2: Two cutlets in one batch in the 12-inch skillet; half the potatoes in a 3-quart pot with 4 cups water.
do_not_scale: oil depth: about 1/4 inch whatever the batch, so the cutlets can float and puff
breading: dredge right before frying, never ahead

Compared with southern-smothered-pork-chops: crisp breaded cutlets, not chops braised in gravy. Compared with kasespatzle-caramelized-onions: a cutlet and potato salad, not cheese noodles.
